title: Changing conditions reveal a principle

captions.emotions: Feeling trust in a meaningful principle

meaning: Ending an exhausted explanation and considering changing conditions can make a principle of comparison clearer within your shared view.
text: Repeated experience may require a familiar explanation to end. Death in the physical position of Ajna ends an exhausted general formula. The Wheel of Fortune in energy considers changing conditions. The Hierophant in emotions feels trust in a meaningful principle. Your view can preserve comparison’s value by recognising that identical names do not establish identical situations, allowing an understood rule to arise from actual distinctions rather than replace consideration of experience.

For example, you stop explaining a walk along one route as invariably tiring. Midday summer heat, evening coolness and different numbers of stops noticeably changed impressions. **Ending a general formula reveals a principle of comparing conditions.** Particular differences become available while the path remains the same. Your view gains understandable foundations: compare significant circumstances as well as names. Trust feels appropriate because the principle explains observations already named. Another walk still need not fit the discovered picture in advance.

The risk is making the principle demand consideration of absolutely everything before any conclusion. Understanding stops before an endless range of conditions. Attention to changing circumstances preserves proportion. Named differences already matter while others may appear later. Your view remains substantial when an old generalisation ends and a grounded particular conclusion becomes possible without promising to encompass every future case beforehand.
